rules: Documentation is not physical verification or a capability grant.
Use actual announced methods, dependencies and resource allowlists.
FIRE GPIO16/17 belongs to PSRAM; keep OS pins and internal I2C devices protected.
An I2C ACK/address alone does not identify a chip or wiring; unknown devices require evidence.
Generic bus access enables future protocols; timing-critical bit banging needs a native adapter or hardware bridge.
Never auto-promote AI guesses, simulation or unconfirmed user reports to physically verified knowledge.

profiles.label: M5 ENV I/II/III/IV/Pro
facts: ENV revisions use different chips; choose the actual model, not just an ACK at the same address.
ENV I: DHT12 0x5c + BMP280 0x76; II: SHT30 0x44 + BMP280 0x76; III: SHT30 0x44 + QMP6988 0x70; IV: SHT40 0x44 + BMP280 0x76; Pro: BME688 0x77.
Use model-specific commands, conversion delays, CRC/calibration and declared external write addresses. Never write internal OS devices.

profiles.label: M5 Unit ADC / ADC v1.1
facts: Original ADC uses ADS1100 (default 0x48); ADC v1.1 uses ADS1110. Confirm revision and address.
Gain, reference and conversion rates differ. Preserve calibration/raw ADC counts; do not assume board GPIO voltage limits match module input range.

profiles.label: M5 INA226 power monitor
facts: INA226-1A and -10A units use I2C 0x41; their shunt values differ (80mOhm vs5mOhm).
Use exact module range/shunt/calibration; never infer wiring, isolation or a safe circuit from an I2C ACK. Raw bus/shunt readings and calibration belong in dataset metadata.

profiles.label: M5 ToF / ToF4M
facts: ToF uses VL53L0X; ToF4M uses VL53L1CXV0FY/1. Both default to0x29 but require different drivers.
Model initialization/ranging is not a single generic register read. Address conflicts need verified enable pins or an I2C multiplexer.

profiles.label: M5 Unit Color
facts: TCS3472, I2C0x29, RGBC measurements; record gain/integration/light configuration with samples.
Shares the default address with ToF; require explicit actual model and bus topology.

profiles.label: M5 Unit DAC
facts: MCP4725 12-bit DAC, I2C0x60. Output changes are physical actions.
Prefer volatile output writes for normal operation; EEPROM persistence is a separate explicit requirement. Confirm output range/load before use.

profiles.label: M5 PaHub I2C expansion
facts: TCA9548A-based six-port PaHub, default I2C0x70; select channel before downstream transactions.
Channel selection and device transaction must remain in the same logical acquisition sequence. Address/topology conflicts are not solved by parallel uncoordinated app writes.

profiles.label: M5 Unit Encoder
facts: STM32-based I2C0x40 module handles the real-time rotary acquisition; Lua reads the module protocol, not raw high-rate GPIO pulses.
Do not confuse encoder registers/LED writes with other 0x40 devices; identify exact unit.

profiles.label: M5 Weight-I2C
facts: STM32+HX711 module uses I2C0x26 and its own documented register protocol.
Tare, calibration, raw ADC count and load-cell setup are separate facts; do not reuse the GPIO-only HX711 interface.

profiles.label: M5 GPIO Weight / bare HX711
facts: Bare HX711/Unit Weight uses clock/data GPIO timing; it is not an I2C register device.
No Lua delay/microsecond bit-banging API is granted. Use an explicitly implemented native timing adapter or a supported I2C bridge/module; normal GPIO calls alone do not establish support.

profiles.label: M5 GPS / UART GNSS
facts: Unit GPS contains AT6558; documented default is9600 baud, no parity, one stop bit. Parse complete frames/checksums and reject invalid fixes.
FIRE has no built-in GPS. Its stock Port C16/17 conflicts with PSRAM; remap to actual announced free pins and verify wiring.

profiles.label: RS485 / Modbus adapter
facts: RS485 requires a suitable electrical transceiver; UART bytes are not RS485 electrical signaling.

Confirm variant, supply, direction control/automatic direction, baud/parity, addressing and protocol CRC. Read-only diagnostic polls first; writes require the requested app behavior. Stock FIRE Port C16/17 is reserved by PSRAM.

profiles.label: M5 COMMU / external CAN
facts: COMMU contains MCP2515 CAN and an RS485 interface. SPI access alone is not a complete CAN driver.
Require correct oscillator/bitrate, transceiver, termination, wiring and OS-approved shared-bus/CS policy. Do not claim a high-level CAN API absent from actual capabilities.

profiles.label: M5 Unit RFID
facts: M5 Unit RFID is an MFRC522-based13.56MHz I2C module at0x28; a generic bare RC522 board may use a different interface.
Use the exact unit protocol. Card reads and writes are separate actions; unavailable keys/card types must not be replaced by fabricated data.

profiles.label: FIRE built-in IMU / vibration
facts: Actual firmware capabilities determine available acceleration/gyro/temperature and Data Engine capture sources. Capture actual timestamps, dropped samples, rate and units.
Requested sampling rate/FPS is not measured uniform sample timing. Spectrum requires valid time basis and an adequate bounded window; do not claim oscilloscope-class bandwidth.

profiles.label: ESP32 BLE tools
facts: ESP32 shares its2.4GHz radio between Wi-Fi and BLE. Bound scan/advertising/GATT work and report busy/unavailable instead of blocking the OS.

Raw advertisements, GATT and classic SPP are different protocols. An encrypted/proprietary light may require pairing/keys; recording packets does not prove replay/control. Only actual advertised methods are allowed.

profiles.label: FIRE GPIO/analog inputs
facts: Only advertised ADC pins are allowed; microphone and other OS pins stay reserved. A disconnected/floating pin is not a valid reference measurement.
ESP32 ADC2 conflicts with active Wi-Fi. Use permitted ADC1/external ADC and actual calibration; never infer volts from raw counts without the configured scale.
